A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same position paper with the same authors and research agenda. Their complete main text, figures, references, and appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix B in v2.

before.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix A report the authors' keyword-based analysis of 62,032 ACL Anthology articles, including publication trends and category totals. These constitute original data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original publication-trend analysis and adds annual absolute counts in Figure 2. Although Section 6 states that no participant experiments were conducted, original bibliometric results are reported.

M1.justification: Both versions present the same conceptual agenda organized around usability, trust, and literacy. Neither introduces an implemented MT algorithm or model, and the revised recommendations do not establish a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: The analyzed corpus remains ACL Anthology articles from 2015 through 2024. Newly cited studies, multimodal examples, and the professional-versus-lay-user table do not introduce populations or tasks actually evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing MT methods or baselines against a proposed system. Additions to the literature discussion are citations rather than new experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the same date range, title/abstract keywords, case-insensitive matching, exclusions, and 62,032-article corpus. Figure 2 supplies annual counts from this analysis without changing the collection or evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, or robustness experiments. Figure 2 presents the existing bibliometric analysis in absolute counts; Appendix B provides conceptual discussion rather than an additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its publication-trend analysis. Discussion of communicating MT uncertainty concerns future system design.

E6.justification: Figure 1's curves and Appendix A's totals remain unchanged: 62,032 articles, including 8,072 MT, 13,977 LM, and 5,084 user-keyword matches. V2 adds annual absolute-count series in Figure 2, providing additional descriptive results from the same corpus.

T1.justification: Neither version contains mathematical propositions, proofs, or formal derivations. Expanded verbal explanations of the three factors and user agency do not introduce new mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The central three-factor agenda is retained, but Section 4 narrows one recommendation: v1 says effective interactions require active users, whereas v2 says users should have the option to participate actively and acknowledges time-sensitive needs.

C2.justification: V2 expands the rationale for selecting the three factors and qualifies the historical account of MT adoption. New Appendix B explains professional/lay distinctions as tendencies along a continuum and identifies limited evidence for finer subgrouping and differences in digital literacy.

D1.justification: V2's introduction adds a repository link for a curated list of the discussed works. V1 has no corresponding resource announcement. The existing Appendix A query instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds early online-MT history, recent human-centered MT work such as Carpuat et al. (2025), and sources on agency and digital literacy. It also replaces Savoldi et al. (2021) with a distinct 2025 review, incrementally updating the existing interdisciplinary positioning.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, retitles and rewrites parts of Section 2, expands the factor-selection explanation, and reorders the limitations paragraphs. It adds acknowledgments and Appendix B while retaining the overall narrative and much of the prose.

P2.justification: V2 expands Figure 1's caption, adds the absolute-count Figure 2, and introduces a six-row professional-versus-lay-user table. The appendices receive separate pages, while the basic two-column design and original trend plot remain.

improvement.justification: V2 better explains the factor selection in Section 5, qualifies expectations for active engagement in Section 4, and clarifies user distinctions and their limits in Appendix B. The supplementary count plot and curated reading list also improve accessibility. These are useful, incremental gains in argumentation and documentation; the central agenda and empirical foundation remain stable.
